summary: After my internship, I continued as a Full Stack Developer and became more involved in production work. I worked on both the frontend and backend, helped improve the admin panel, optimized performance, fixed production issues, and participated in deploying updates. The role gave me a much better understanding of how real applications are maintained after they go live.
highlights: Promoted from internship into a full-time development role
Worked across frontend, backend and production deployments
Improved application performance for real users
Built features used in the live production platform
Collaborated on debugging and production releases
challenge: The biggest challenge was improving performance without changing how the website worked for users. Blog pages were loading slowly because of large images and repeated API requests. I redesigned the fetching flow, introduced browser-side caching, optimized image delivery, and tested changes across different devices to make sure the improvements were consistent.
contributions: Built new pages and production features using React
Developed backend API functionality with Node.js
Improved the admin dashboard and blog management workflow
Integrated Firebase Authentication into user flows
Reduced unnecessary API requests through client-side caching
Optimized image loading across media-heavy pages
Resolved responsive layout issues across multiple devices
Participated in deployment and production monitoring
results: Reduced repeated blog requests by approximately 68%
Improved average blog page load times by roughly 70%
Delivered more than 12 production features and improvements
Resolved over 25 production issues across different browsers and devices
Improved responsiveness and overall user experience

summary: This was my first professional backend role and where I became comfortable working in a production codebase. I spent most of my time building REST APIs, fixing backend issues, improving existing services, and learning how larger applications are structured. It also helped me understand how teams review, test, and release software.
highlights: Worked on a production ASP.NET Core backend
Built and improved REST API endpoints
challenge: One of the harder parts was understanding a codebase that already had multiple layers and dependencies. Before making changes, I spent time tracing request flow through controllers, services, repositories, and the database so I could fix problems without introducing new ones.
contributions: Developed backend APIs using ASP.NET Core and C#
Implemented business logic and request validation
Worked with SQL Server and Redis
Debugged issues across controllers and services
results: Resolved more than 40 backend issues during development
Reduced recurring defects before production releases
Improved backend maintainability through cleaner service organization
Helped support thousands of application requests each day
